newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-French stocks jump two percent, dollar soft.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French stocks jump two percent, dollar soft.

text.p: European financial markets opened mixed on Thursday, but French shares bucked lacklustre conditions across much of the region by carving out a strong early gain.
The dollar and bond markets softened across the board with traders predicting a relatively quiet day ahead of key U.S. jobless data due on Friday that might point the way for American interest rates.
However, lingering concerns over European economic and monetary union (EMU) and Germany's budget problems were seen providing some support for the dollar against the mark.

On the precious metals market, palladium prices jumped to a record fixing and platinum reached its highest fix in nearly two years as dealers scrambled for metal in acute short supply due to a five-month suspension of Russian exports.
The Russians, the world's largest suppliers of palladium, are expected to resume supplies in late June, but stockpiles have been run down in the meantime.

Despite the Bonn government's climbdown in the face of opposition from the powerful Bundesbank to its plan to revalue the nation's reserves, German press commentators said the crisis was far from over.

But German share traders said the market was relieved that a solution appeared to have been found to the dispute over the government's efforts to plug a hole in its finances in order to qualify for monetary union.
"The important thing is that they seem to have found an amicable solution," said Josh Waiblinger, assistant vice president of equities at BHF-Bank, as the DAX index opened with modest gains.

There was little reaction to first quarter German GDP data, which showed growth of 0.5 percent from the previous quarter and 1.4 percent year-on-year. The figures were slightly ahead of some expectations but not enough to pressure the market, dealers said.
Interest was focused on individual stocks, with Deutsche Bank AG remaining in vogue, 83 pfennigs up at 99.48 marks by 0930 GMT.
French shares posted gains of more than two percent in the morning, helped by the dollar and the strength of the futures market.

The nomination of a left-wing government on Wednesday with a Communist transport minister did not make a big difference to the market. Investors were reassured by the government's commitment to the euro with the naming of Dominique Strauss-Kahn as finance minister, dealers said.
Brokers said investors were now waiting for the government's policy statements.
Among individual shares, Sanofi jumped 6.4 percent to 549 francs following Wednesday's bullish profit forecast.
Wall Street's weak overnight performance, which saw the Dow lose 42 points to 7,269, weighed on the London market in early trade.
The FTSE 100 index was down 9.7 points at 4,547.4 by 0915 GMT. Retailer Boots fell 18 pence to 676 as the stock went ex a special dividend, while profit-taking continued to hit bank shares.
"It is all looking a bit nasty at the moment," said one dealer. "The big players are on the sidelines keeping their powder dry and there are one or two lines of stock on offer."

Dealers said the market was focused on Friday's first meeting of the newly-appointed Bank of England monetary policy committee that must decide whether to raise interest rates to slow down the pace of economic growth.
A Reuters survey showed 12 out of 21 economists expected a quarter point rise in the British base lending rate to 6.50 percent.
Back on the foreign exchange market, traders pushed the dollar down to near its session lows around 1.7250 marks after becoming frustrated at their failure to make gains on the upside.

"The market's a bit fed up with trying to take the dollar higher, so we'll have a look at the downside and see if there are any stops around," said Nick Probert, head of spot trading at Bank of America in London.
CURRENCIES AT 0920 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7247 marks and 115.71 yen compared with 1.7310 marks and 116.23 yen in late European trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0920 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 9.7 points, or 0.21 percent, at 4,723.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 53.9 points, or 2.05 percent, at 2,689.27.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 10 points, or 0.27 percent, at 3,671.84.
PRECIOUS METALS
Palladium fixed at $235.00 an ounce, up from $208.00 on Wednesday. Platinum fixed at $440.00, its highest level since September 15, 1995.
Gold was quoted at $341.45 in early trade compared with the London close of $342.35. Silver was three cents lower at $4.73.
